issues.finding: D gets the highest partial credit (.35) despite bypassing mandatory access control. A (.20) and B (.30) fail to release a record but preserve the hard access gate. No time penalty or impact makes that breach the better runner-up. D WHEN allows opening an empty record but gives no reason to prefer it over C, which also meets that permission.
issues.fix: Price the hard gate consistently. Prefer a viable partial action which preserves access control while incompletely addressing the cycle; give it the runner-up position. For D WHEN, establish a positive requirement to provide immediate client access before attachment and explicit permission to do so.

issues.scope: A versus C as diagnostic options and DQ; B counterfactual
issues.finding: A and C both start immediately, trigger the same automatic retry, finish refund at minute 5 and expose the same double debit. A plans to return later, but the retry happens before then; C delegates precisely what the system does anyway. The consequences provide no basis for .25 versus .20, and C WHEN with safe automated reconciliation also makes A defensible. B WHEN revokes urgency but does not specify whether the ordinary queue / planned review can honor or replace the agreed deadline.
issues.fix: Give C a distinct decision with meaningful advantage, limitation and counterfactual, then set partial credit from demonstrated trade-offs. In B WHEN specify changed/agreed deadline and a feasible ordinary queue/review. Justify relative cost of B versus inducing a repeated debit (B currently scores lowest).
